stem:
The diagram shows two rays drawn from a common point O on Tara's slate: ray OA and ray OB.

Which statement correctly describes the angle they form?

options.text: The vertex of the angle is arm OA.
OA and OB form this angle even if they start at two different points.
The rays share starting point O (the vertex); the arms are OA and OB; the angle may be named $\angle AOB$.
The angle is named $\angle O$ because O is the first letter printed on the slate.

teacher.key_rationale: An angle needs two arms from one vertex. C names vertex O and arms OA, OB. A swaps vertex with an arm. B drops the common-point condition. D grabs the printed letter O.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote right triangle into two rays from O with a marked angle; stem refers to the diagram.
